examples.text: Ты что здесь вообще сейчас делаешь?
examples.trans: What on earth are you doing here right now?

examples.text: Я делаю выбор не разумом и не желудком.
examples.trans: I am making the choice not with my mind and not with my stomach.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Костя, я вчера и сам испугался.
examples.trans: Kostya, I got scared myself yesterday too.

examples.text: Ты сам эту кашу заварил.
examples.trans: You stirred up this mess yourself.

examples.text: Я же сказала, решай проблемы сам.
examples.trans: I already told you, solve your problems yourself.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'porridge', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Ты сам эту кашу заварил.
examples.trans: You stirred up this mess yourself.

examples.text: Я пойду попробую приготовить себе кашу.
examples.trans: I will go try to cook myself some porridge.

examples.text: Дети едят кашу по утрам.
examples.trans: Children eat porridge in the mornings.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (root 'варить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'brew'.

examples.text: Ты сам эту кашу заварил.
examples.trans: You stirred up this mess yourself.

examples.text: Заварите мне ещё одну чашку.
examples.trans: Brew me one more cup.

examples.text: Ой, остыл совсем, я свежий заварю.
examples.trans: Oh, it has gone cold. I will brew a fresh pot.
